Definition: literally, sevened, i.e. a week (specifically, of years)
BiblicalUsage: A shabu'a is a week, literally a seven, and Scripture counts time by it in both directions. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, counted as a week of years, and Moses told Israel to count seven weeks to the feast of weeks. Daniel's vision stretches the same word across history, with seventy weeks determined upon Jerusalem, seven of them reaching to Messiah the Prince.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God counts time in sevens because He ordered it that way from the beginning. The seventy weeks tell me that history is not drifting, it is measured, and the coming of Messiah fell exactly where God said it would. That is why I trust His timing even when I cannot see the calendar He is using.
